import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 888

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/888](https://www.erdosproblems.com/888)
- [Er98] Erdős, Paul, Some of my new and almost new problems and results in combinatorial number
  theory. Number theory (Eger, 1996) (1998), 169-180.
-/

open Filter

namespace Erdos888

/--
Condition on the sets $A$ appearing in Erdős 888. Namely, let $A$ be a subset
of ${1,...,n}$ such that if $a ≤ b ≤ c ≤ d ∈ A$ and $abcd$ square then $ad=bc$.
-/
def RequiredCondition (A : Finset ℕ) (n : ℕ) : Prop :=
  A ⊆ Finset.Ioc 0 n ∧ ∀ᵉ (a ∈ A) (b ∈ A) (c ∈ A) (d ∈ A),
  a ≤ b → b ≤ c → c ≤ d → IsSquare (a * b * c * d) → a * d = b * c

/--
Proposition that for a specific $n$ an $A$ with the above defined condition and cardinality $k$
exists.
-/
def p (n : ℕ) (k : ℕ) : Prop := ∃ A : Finset ℕ, RequiredCondition A n ∧ A.card = k

open scoped Classical in
/--
What is the size of the largest $A\subseteq \{1,\ldots,n\}$ such that if
$a\leq b\leq c\leq d\in A$ are such that $abcd$ is a square then $ad=bc$?

This was proved by GPT-5.5 Pro (prompted by Chojecki).
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11,
  formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/dfe2d78128b493c572cf525b1b8edf4897fb7664/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos888.lean#L47"]
theorem erdos_888 :
    (fun n : ℕ ↦ (Nat.findGreatest (p n) n : ℝ)) =Θ[atTop]
      (fun n : ℕ ↦ (n : ℝ) * Real.log (Real.log n) / Real.log n) := by
  sorry

open scoped Classical in
/--
Erdős claims that Sárközy proved that $\lvert A\rvert =o(n)$ (a proof of this
bound is provided by Tao in the comments).
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_888.variants.sarkozy :
    (fun n ↦ (Nat.findGreatest (p n) n : ℝ)) =o[atTop] (Nat.cast : ℕ → ℝ) := by
  sorry

open scoped Classical in
/--
The primes show that $\lvert A\rvert \gg n/\log n$ is possible.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_888.variants.primes :
    (fun n : ℕ ↦ (Nat.findGreatest (p n) n : ℝ)) ≫ (fun n : ℕ ↦ (n : ℝ) / Real.log n) := by
  sorry

open scoped Classical in
/--
Cambie and Weisenberg have noted in the comments that the set of semiprimes
also works, showing $(1+o(1))\frac{\log\log n}{\log n}n \leq \lvert A\rvert$ is achievable.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_888.variants.semiprimes :
    (fun n : ℕ ↦ (Nat.findGreatest (p n) n : ℝ)) ≫
      (fun n : ℕ ↦ (n : ℝ) * Real.log (Real.log n) / Real.log n) := by
  sorry

end Erdos888

findings.description: The `≫` conclusion at lines 86–87 loses the leading constant 1 in the cited lower bound. Writing F(n) for the bounded maximum and g(n) = n log(log n)/log n, the Lean statement means that some c > 0 satisfies c·g(n) ≤ F(n) eventually. The source instead gives F(n) ≥ (1+o(1))g(n), requiring (1−ε)g(n) ≤ F(n) eventually for every ε > 0. These are not equivalent asymptotic assertions. In /workspace/review/asymptotic.lean, I proved, using this actual comparison scale, that g/2 satisfies the `≫` relation but fails the coefficient-1 lower bound at ε = 1/4. The existing theorem is a valid weaker corollary, not the sharp lower bound its docstring states.
findings.source_evidence: https://www.erdosproblems.com/888 explicitly says that `(1+o(1)) (log log n/log n)n ≤ |A|` is achievable. Desmond Weisenberg's comment https://www.erdosproblems.com/forum/thread/888#post-121 states the same coefficient-1 bound. Proposition 3.1 of https://www.ulam.ai/research/erdos888.pdf likewise states F(n) ≥ |B(n)| = (1+o(1))n log log n/log n.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the conclusion with `∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, (1 - ε) * ((n : ℝ) * Real.log (Real.log n) / Real.log n) ≤ (Nat.findGreatest (p n) n : ℝ)`. This preserves a lower bound rather than incorrectly requiring asymptotic equality of the maximum. The existing `≫` statement can remain as a separately documented weaker corollary.

findings.description: The explanatory construction at lines 81–82 should say squarefree semiprimes, not all semiprimes. Under the usual definition, semiprimes include prime squares. The pair {4,9} already violates `RequiredCondition`: the ordered quadruple (4,4,4,9) has product 24², but 4·9 ≠ 4·4. I proved `¬ RequiredCondition {4,9} 9` in /workspace/review/computations.lean. This is a correction to the explanatory construction; excluding prime squares does not change the asserted asymptotic lower bound.
findings.source_evidence: Although the problem page's summary uses the same shorthand, the underlying comment https://www.erdosproblems.com/forum/thread/888#post-121 explicitly says 'the entire set of semiprimes (excluding primes squared), together with the primes'. Cambie's comment #post-103 specifies products of two different primes. Proposition 3.1 of https://www.ulam.ai/research/erdos888.pdf uses B(n) = {primes ≤ n} ∪ {pq ≤ n : p < q primes}.
findings.suggested_fix: Change 'the set of semiprimes also works' to 'the set of squarefree semiprimes also works', optionally mentioning that primes may also be included.

reformulations.difference: The source discusses the largest admissible subset and two-sided order-of-magnitude bounds; Lean uses `Nat.findGreatest (p n) n` and includes n = 0.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Every admissible set has cardinality at most n because `Finset.Ioc 0 n` has n elements. The empty set is admissible, so `p n 0` always holds. Thus the bounded search really attains the maximum and never relies on an unattained default value. I proved its maximum characterization and its equality with an explicit finite enumeration. I also proved that Θ of this maximum is equivalent to eventual positive-constant lower constructions together with a uniform upper bound for every admissible set. The logarithmic scale is eventually positive, and including n = 0 does not affect atTop asymptotics.

reformulations.difference: The source's statement that admissible sets satisfy |A| = o(n) is expressed as little-o of the maximum cardinality, without explicitly quantifying over admissible sets.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Since the maximum is attained and bounds every admissible cardinality, its little-o assertion is equivalent to: for every ε > 0, eventually in n, every admissible A has |A| ≤ εn. This exact equivalence was proved as `Review888.littleO_max_iff_uniform` in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

The pinned external main theorem and foundational definitions match the repository statement; its supporting source files were inspected, but the separate external project was not rebuilt. The other explicitly cited source, its detailed comments and the linked solution supplied precise statements for the review. Scratch proofs compile without sorryAx; computed maxima for n = 0 through 12 are 0,1,2,3,3,4,5,6,6,6,7,8,8, agreeing with OEIS at positive indices. All experiments are under /workspace/review/, and the reviewed file's hash still matches the specified commit.

submission.summary: Replaced the unspecified-constant lower bound with the sharp statement that, for every ε > 0, the maximum is eventually at least (1 − ε)n log(log n)/log n. Also clarified the docstring to specify squarefree semiprimes. No other declarations were changed. The requested compile command succeeds with only the existing `declaration uses 'sorry'` warnings.
